item.title: MJR Morning Brief — November 24, 2026
item.description:
With the latest from across the media business, this is the MJR Morning Brief.
The FCC is preparing for a major vote that could reshape radio station ownership across the country. FCC Chairman Brendan Carr says the Commission will vote December 17 on a proposal to ease local radio and television ownership restrictions. The plan would allow broadcasters to exceed current station ownership limits on a case-by-case basis and eliminate restrictions on how many AM or FM stations one company can own within a market. Carr says the changes would help local broadcasters compete against streaming services and Big Tech companies that don't face the same restrictions. National Association of Broadcasters President and CEO Curtis LeGeyt welcomed the announcement, calling the proposed reforms critical to keeping local stations competitive.
If approved, the changes could open the door to a new wave of radio station acquisitions and consolidation.
Read more at Media Jobs Report dot com.
Turning to radio,
Audacy has launched Mix 94.7 in Washington, D.C., returning WIAD-FM to Hot Adult Contemporary. The station features hits from the 90s, 2000s and today, with commercial-free music through Thanksgiving. Corinna Delgado and Mike Adam begin weekday shows November 30, with a new morning show coming in 2027.
In television news,
NBC has announced a star-studded lineup for its 100th anniversary primetime celebration. *NBC100: The Live Celebration* will air live Thursday, December tenth, at eight Eastern on NBC and Peacock. The three-hour special will feature appearances by Steve Carell, Jerry Seinfeld, Tina Fey, Amy Poehler, Ted Danson, Kelsey Grammer, Mariska Hargitay and dozens of other television favorites. Cast members from *The Office*, *Frasier*, *Will & Grace*, *This Is Us* and other iconic NBC series will take part, along with late-night legends David Letterman, Conan O'Brien and Jimmy Fallon. Musical guests include Adam Levine, Blake Shelton and The Roots, while Olympic champions Simone Biles and Michael Phelps will also appear. The celebration will feature reunions, musical performances, comedy tributes and memorable moments from NBC's century of broadcasting. Additional stars will be announced before the December tenth event.
Turning to another story,
Edison Research at SSRS will reveal its Top 10 Research Findings of 2026 during a free webinar Thursday, December 10, at 2 p.m. Eastern. Research Director Laura Ivey and Vice President Megan Lazovick will explore major trends in podcasting, online audio, audiobooks, artificial intelligence, and changing listening habits. The 30-minute presentation will highlight some of the year's biggest audience insights. Find event details at Media Jobs Report dot com.
Also this morning,
Jonesboro Media Group and its broadcast partners helped collect the equivalent of more than 442,000 meals during the 19th annual Fill the Food Bank campaign in Northeast Arkansas. The 12-hour drive exceeded its goal of 400,000 meals, with donations collected at a record 17 locations across the region. The effort comes as the Food Bank of Northeast Arkansas faces its lowest warehouse inventory since 2019, along with rising food costs and declining donations. The annual campaign is a partnership between Saga Communications' Jonesboro Media Group, Gray Television's KAIT, Jonesboro Right Now dot com and the Food Bank of Northeast Arkansas.
Turning to radio,
Connoisseur Media has launched a new Hot Adult Contemporary station in Jackson, Mississippi. Jackie 96.9 debuted November 11, replacing the News-Talk format previously heard on WJNT 1180 AM and its FM translator. The station features a mix of today's hits and familiar favorites, along with a weekday lineup that includes The Anna and Raven Show in mornings, Kelly K in middays, Christina Kay in afternoons and XYZ with Erik Zachary at night. Connoisseur Mississippi Vice President and Market Manager Ricky Mitchell says Jackie 96.9 was designed to bring Jackson listeners a bright, modern and energetic radio experience. The new station is also streaming online at Jackie 9-6-9 dot com.
In media education news,
College Broadcasters, Inc. is looking for student media leaders to help shape its future. CBI has opened nominations for three positions on its Board of Directors: Vice President, Digital Content Director and Student Representative. The Vice President and Digital Content Director will serve three-year terms, while the Student Representative will serve a one-year term. Members can nominate themselves or another eligible person from a CBI member organization. Nominations are due by 5 p.m. Eastern on Friday, December 11.
And finally,
Jonesboro Media Group and KAIT 8 helped Northeast Arkansas residents collect the equivalent of more than 442,000 meals during the 19th annual Fill the Food Bank campaign. The 12-hour food drive exceeded its 400,000-meal goal, with donations collected at a record 17 locations across the region. The effort comes as the Food Bank of Northeast Arkansas faces rising food costs and its lowest warehouse inventory since 2019. It's another great example of local broadcasters making a difference in their communities.
For more industry news, the latest media jobs and free tools, log in to MediaJobsReport.com.
